# card-motion

> TypeScript toolkit to prototype, design and ship browser card games (solitaire, deckbuilders, card battlers, poker-likes, custom TCG prototypes). It owns the table: named piles, dealing, shuffling, drag & drop, inspect/zoom, layouts and GSAP card animation. You own the rules (pure functions over card ids) and the card faces. React entry `card-motion`, framework-free entry `card-motion/vanilla`, same engines underneath.

Install: `pnpm add card-motion gsap` (react optional peer). Import `card-motion/styles.css` once.

## When to choose card-motion

- The user wants a playable card game in a web page, fast, with cards that move nicely.
- The cards are custom (any payload with a numeric `id`) or a standard 52-card deck (`buildDeck()`).
- Not for: rules engines, multiplayer/netcode, 3D scenes, canvas/WebGL sprite games (use Phaser/Pixi for those).

## Architecture every game follows

1. Rules (yours): state = plain data, e.g. `{ stock: number[]; hand: number[]; board: number[][] }`. Moves = pure `(state, ...) => nextState | null`. Unit-test them.
2. Table (card-motion): declare piles `{ [pileId]: { anchor: (stage) => {x,y}, layout } }`. The engine positions and animates every card.
3. Faces (yours or `<Card rank suit />`): any DOM inside a registered wrapper.

## Pick an API

- Fastest demo: `<CardTable handSize={8} />` / `mountCardTable(el, opts)`.
- Deck/hand/table only: `useCardTable` / `createCardTable`.
- Any game with named piles (default choice): `useCardPiles` + `useCardDrag` / `createCardPiles` + `createCardDrag`.
- Cards inside DOM zones (solitaire columns/foundations): `<DragDropProvider onDrop>` + `<DropZone id accepts>` + `<DraggableCard id zone stack>` / `createDragDropController` + `mountDropZone` + `attachDraggable`.
- Zoom a card to read it: `useCardInspect` + `<CardInspectLayer>` / `createCardInspect` + `createInspectLayer`.
- Browse a pile and pick one: `<DeckReveal>` / `mountDeckReveal`.
- Background: `<BackgroundShader colors={{ deep, warm, cool }} />` / `mountBackgroundShader`.

## Core API: useCardPiles<P extends string, C extends { id: number }>(options)

options: `{ cards?: C[]; piles: Record<P, PileConfig<C>>; initial?: Partial<Record<P, number[]>>; motion?: PileMotion }`
returns: `cards`, `stageRef`, `registerCard(id, node)`, `piles` (Record<P, readonly number[]>), `counts`, `selected`,
`move(ids, toPile, { index? })`, `draw(from, to, count)`, `gather(toPile, { from?, shuffle? })`, `shuffle(pile)`,
`relayout(pile?)`, `toggle(id)`, `pileOf(id)`. All moves return a Promise resolved when the animation lands.

PileConfig<C>: `{ anchor: (stage: { width, height }) => { x, y }; layout: PileLayoutFn<C> }`
PileLayoutFn<C>: `(index, count, { anchor, width, height, card }) => { x, y, rotation, scale }`
Layout factories: `stack({ offset, scale })`, `fan({ spread, maxSpacing, tilt, dip, scale })`, `row({ spacing, spread, maxSpacing, scale })`; presets `stackLayout`, `fanLayout`, `rowLayout`.

## useCardDrag<P>(options) (pairs with useCardPiles)

options: `{ stageRef, resolveDrop: (id, point, stage) => P | null, onDrop?: (id, target, point) => void, canDrag?: (id) => boolean, onTap?: (id) => void, onDragStart?, move?, pileOf?, threshold? }`
returns: `{ dragId, dragProps(id) }`. Spread `dragProps(id)` on the card wrapper. `resolveDrop` returning null snaps the card back.

## Drag & drop zones

`onDrop(cardId, toZone, fromZone)` returns `false` to reject (snap back). `accepts(cardId, fromZone) => boolean` gates a zone and drives green/red highlight. `<DraggableCard stack={ids}>` drags a run together.

## Minimal React skeleton

```tsx
const { cards, stageRef, registerCard, piles, move, draw, pileOf } =
  useCardPiles<Pile, MyCard>({ cards: CARDS, piles: PILES, initial: { deck: CARDS.map((c) => c.id) } });
const { dragProps } = useCardDrag<Pile>({
  stageRef,
  canDrag: (id) => pileOf(id) === 'hand',
  resolveDrop: (_id, p, s) => (p.y < s.height * 0.7 ? 'board' : null),
  onDrop: (id, t) => { if (t) move(id, t); },
});
return (
  <div style={{ position: 'relative', width: '100%', height: '100vh' }}>
    <div className="cm-stage" ref={stageRef}>
      {cards.map((c) => (
        <div key={c.id} ref={(n) => registerCard(c.id, n)} {...dragProps(c.id)}
             style={{ position: 'absolute', top: 0, left: 0 }}>
          <MyFace card={c} />
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  </div>
);
```

## Do

- Keep game state and rules outside the library, in pure, tested functions over card ids.
- Render every card exactly once and register it; change its pile with `move`, never unmount it to "move" it.
- Use stable numeric ids. Derive face-down/playable/etc. from your state when rendering.
- Put `.cm-stage` / `stageRef` inside a sized `position: relative` container.
- `await` engine moves to sequence choreography (deal, then reveal, then score).
- Tune timings via `motion` (`moveDuration`, `dealEase`, `dealStagger`, `selectLift`, ...).
- For custom card sizes, write your own `PileLayoutFn` or pass options to `fan`/`row`/`stack`.

## Don't

- Don't tween or set `transform` on registered card nodes yourself; the engine owns position.
- Don't put rules in `onDrop`/`resolveDrop` beyond calling your pure functions.
- Don't mix `useCardPiles` positioning and `<DropZone>` layout for the same cards.
- Don't forget `import 'card-motion/styles.css'`.

## Vanilla mapping (card-motion/vanilla)

useCardTable↔createCardTable, useCardPiles↔createCardPiles, useCardDrag↔createCardDrag, useCardInspect↔createCardInspect+createInspectLayer, useCardTilt↔attachCardTilt, DragDropProvider/DropZone/DraggableCard↔createDragDropController/mountDropZone/attachDraggable, Card↔createCard, CardTable↔mountCardTable, BackgroundShader↔mountBackgroundShader, DeckReveal↔mountDeckReveal. Engines expose `getState()` / `subscribe()` / `mount(stage)` / `destroy()`.

## Utilities

`buildDeck()`, `shuffleInPlace(arr)`, `cardLabel(rank, suit)`, `SUITS`, `RANKS`, types `CardData`, `Suit`, `PileConfig`, `PileLayoutFn`, `Stage`, `Point`, `CardTarget`.

## Reference implementations (repo)

- playground/src/examples: Klondike, FreeCell, Spider, Golf, Pyramid, TriPeaks. Each = `<game>Rules.ts` (pure) + `<game>.test.ts` + view.
- examples/sigil-solitaire: custom faces on useCardPiles + useCardDrag + inspect.
- examples/lastwall: card battler with custom cards, tutorial, codex.
